items.headline: Workers' Party keeps Pritam Singh as chief in a special cadre confidence vote
items.summary: About 79% of the 107 cadres present at a special conference on 28 June voted to retain Pritam Singh as Workers' Party secretary-general, after which he was re-elected unopposed; senior counsel Harpreet Singh was the sole new face on the party's central executive committee.

items.headline: Singapore's new Online Safety Commission opens, letting victims file harm reports online
items.summary: The Online Safety Commission began operations on 29 June under the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act, allowing victims to file free reports at osc.gov.sg against five online harms including doxxing, harassment and image-based abuse.

items.headline: Stars Engrg director jailed over the 2021 Tuas blast that killed three workers
items.summary: Director Chua Xing Da, 42, was jailed 18 months and one week and the firm fined S$500,000 over the February 2021 Tuas Avenue 11 explosion that killed three and injured seven.

items.headline: Singapore think-tank issues a rare 'red' haze alert for the August-September peak
items.summary: The Singapore Institute of International Affairs gave its highest 'red' rating in its 2026 Haze Outlook, warning of severe transboundary haze with August to September the period of greatest danger.

items.headline: Modi gifts Seychelles a made-in-India patrol vessel and a 1,250-crore credit line
items.summary: On a state visit for Seychelles' National Day golden jubilee, PM Narendra Modi handed over the made-in-India fast patrol vessel PS Lespwar plus ambulances and utility vehicles, extended a 1,250-crore-rupee line of credit, and became the first Indian PM to address the Seychelles National Assembly.

items.headline: CBI's Operation Chakra-VI raids 80-plus sites in 16 states over 'digital arrest' scams
items.summary: The CBI searched more than 80 locations across 16 states and arrested two people in a crackdown on 'digital arrest' fraud networks linked to over 200 cases, uncovering a fake website mimicking the Supreme Court of India.

items.headline: Amarnath Yatra's Pratham Puja held as security tightens before the 3 July start
items.summary: The ceremonial Pratham Puja for the Amarnath Yatra was performed on 29 June ahead of the 57-day pilgrimage beginning 3 July; authorities made RFID cards mandatory, doubled accident insurance to 10 lakh rupees and deployed Project Hawk Eye.

items.headline: Centre reappoints RBI Deputy Governor Swaminathan Janakiraman for two more years
items.summary: The government extended the tenure of Reserve Bank of India Deputy Governor Swaminathan Janakiraman by two years from 26 June 2026, keeping the former State Bank of India executive in a role overseeing key portfolios until 2028.

items.headline: South East Water orders a Kent hosepipe ban for 850,000 customers from 3 July
items.summary: South East Water announced a temporary use ban affecting about 850,000 customers in Kent, formally in force from 3 July but urged immediately, after record June demand during the heatwave; breaches carry fines of up to 1,000 pounds.

items.headline: Update: Reeves backs Burnham as the Labour leadership race heads toward a coronation
items.summary: Chancellor Rachel Reeves endorsed Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham to succeed Keir Starmer while urging him to keep her economic plan, leaving Burnham the clear front-runner with backing from more than 200 MPs; nominations open on 9 July.

items.headline: UK retail sales slump deepens as consumer confidence holds at minus 23
items.summary: The CBI's Distributive Trades Survey found June retail sales volumes below seasonal norms by the most in over two years, while GfK's consumer confidence index stayed at minus 23.

items.headline: Reform UK extends its polling lead over Labour and the Conservatives
items.summary: Polling averages put Reform UK first on about 26%, ahead of Labour on roughly 21% and the Conservatives near 19%, as Labour's leadership crisis weighs on the party's standing.

items.headline: DR Congo files a case against Rwanda at the World Court over decades of alleged abuses
items.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo lodged a case at the International Court of Justice accusing Rwanda of more than 30 years of massacres, sexual violence and forced displacement.

items.headline: Update: Hezbollah rejects the US-brokered Israel-Lebanon deal as 'null and void'
items.summary: Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem rejected the US-mediated Israel-Lebanon framework signed in Washington, calling it 'null and void' and a surrender of sovereignty over its provision tying an Israeli withdrawal to the group's disarmament; Hezbollah said it will not disarm.

items.headline: Morocco jails 29, including politicians and sports figures, in a major drug trial
items.summary: A Moroccan court handed prison terms of up to 12 years to 29 defendants, among them prominent politicians and sports figures, concluding a two-year drug-trafficking and corruption case.

items.headline: USMCA faces a make-or-break review on 1 July as Trump hints he may not renew it
items.summary: The US-Mexico-Canada trade pact reaches its first mandatory joint review on 1 July amid business uncertainty, after President Trump signalled he may not renew the deal; US negotiators are pushing to raise regional auto-content requirements to 82%.

items.headline: Apple lobbies Washington to buy memory chips from blacklisted Chinese maker CXMT
items.summary: Apple is pressing the US Commerce Department to approve sourcing DRAM from ChangXin Memory Technologies, which sits on a Pentagon military-company list, as it tries to contain surging AI-driven memory costs.

items.headline: A startup founder used Anthropic's Claude to read his cancer scans and skip radiotherapy
items.summary: TechCrunch reported that a founder fed his medical scans to Claude, which estimated a roughly 90% chance his thymus had reactivated after chemotherapy rather than active disease; a specialist later confirmed the thymus rebound.

items.headline: AI networking startup Netris raises a $15 million Series A led by a16z
items.summary: Network-automation startup Netris raised $15 million led by Andreessen Horowitz after reporting 800% annual recurring revenue growth and more than 35 live GPU-cluster deployments.

items.headline: Menlo Ventures raises a record $3 billion fund on the strength of its Anthropic bet
items.summary: Menlo Ventures closed a $3 billion fund, the largest in its five-decade history, driven by its AI portfolio; the firm's stake in Anthropic is now valued at about $14 billion.

items.headline: SoftBank shares plunge over 12% on a report OpenAI may delay its IPO to 2027
items.summary: SoftBank Group fell as much as 14% intraday and closed down more than 12% at 6,226 yen after a report that OpenAI could push its listing to 2027; it was the stock's worst day since August 2024.

items.headline: Cyber firm Varonis weighs a sale after takeover interest from Blackstone and Thoma Bravo
items.summary: Varonis Systems is exploring a sale with advisers after fielding preliminary interest from private-equity firms including Blackstone, Thoma Bravo and Vista Equity Partners; its shares jumped about 12%.

items.headline: FedEx beats with $25 billion in quarterly revenue but shares slide about 6%
items.summary: FedEx reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $25 billion and adjusted earnings of $6.31 a share, topping estimates, yet shares fell roughly 6% after hours on a cautious outlook.

items.headline: Qualcomm is in advanced talks to buy AI-software firm Modular for about $4 billion
items.summary: Bloomberg reported that Qualcomm is negotiating to acquire AI-infrastructure software company Modular in a deal valued at roughly $4 billion, part of a push beyond smartphones into data-center AI.

items.headline: 🏎️ Russell holds off Verstappen to win the Austrian Grand Prix
items.summary: George Russell converted pole into victory at the Red Bull Ring, finishing 1.611s ahead of Max Verstappen with Kimi Antonelli third, ending a months-long winless run.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli stays top of the standings as F1 heads to a Silverstone sprint
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli leads the drivers' championship on 171 points after finishing third in Austria, with Russell's win lifting him to second, 40 points back; the next round is the British Grand Prix at Silverstone, a sprint weekend, on 5 July.

items.headline: 🎾 Sinner opens his Wimbledon title defence against Kecmanovic as the draw begins
items.summary: Defending champion Jannik Sinner starts on Centre Court against Miomir Kecmanovic as Wimbledon's main draw opens on 29 June, with Aryna Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic also in Day 1 action.

items.headline: 🎾 Serena Williams returns on a wildcard as Alcaraz misses Wimbledon injured
items.summary: Seven-time champion Serena Williams plays Wimbledon on a singles wildcard, her first singles appearance since the 2022 US Open, while Carlos Alcaraz is absent with a wrist injury that has sidelined him since April.

items.headline: 🏏 Australia knock India out of the Women's T20 World Cup with a six-wicket win
items.summary: Australia chased down 171 with an over to spare to beat India by six wickets at Lord's, ending India's hopes; Ellyse Perry made 56 off 38 and Ashleigh Gardner finished 53 not out off 29 after Harmanpreet Kaur's 56.

items.headline: 🏏 Women's T20 World Cup semi-finals set as Australia and South Africa seal spots
items.summary: The last four are confirmed as Australia, England, South Africa and West Indies after the group stage, with Australia and South Africa winning their final fixtures to qualify; hosts England finished unbeaten.

items.headline: Great apes and humans have laughed to the same beat for 15 million years
items.summary: Analysing 140 laughter sequences from humans, chimpanzees, bonobos, gorillas and orangutans, researchers found all five species laugh with the same evenly spaced rhythm, suggesting the vocal control behind laughter began evolving about 15 million years ago.

items.headline: Gene-editing's next act: switching genes off without cutting DNA
items.summary: Nature reports that several startups are advancing first-in-human epigenetic-editing therapies that silence genes rather than cut them, aiming to treat conditions from high cholesterol to muscular dystrophy.

items.headline: Hubble spots an early galaxy clearing the universe's primordial fog
items.summary: Astronomers using the Hubble Space Telescope detected ultraviolet light escaping a galaxy that existed just 1.4 billion years after the Big Bang, evidence that compact, star-forming galaxies helped burn off the early universe's hydrogen fog.

items.headline: Scientists build the first ticking 'nuclear clocks'
items.summary: Two research teams have demonstrated the first working nuclear clocks, a long-sought timekeeper based on an energy transition inside the nucleus of thorium-229 that could one day outperform today's best atomic clocks.

fun_fact.headline: Bubble wrap was originally invented as textured wallpaper, not packaging
fun_fact.body: Bubble wrap was never meant for packaging. In 1957, engineers Alfred Fielding and Marc Chavannes sealed two plastic shower curtains together while trying to invent a trendy textured wallpaper. The wallpaper flopped, but in 1961 IBM began using the bubbly sheets to protect a new computer in transit, and the inventors' company went on to become the packaging giant Sealed Air.
fun_fact.source: Smithsonian Magazine; New Jersey Inventors Hall of Fame

puzzle.title: The Last Ball
puzzle.body: A bag holds 7 black balls and 8 white balls. You repeatedly remove two balls at random: if they are the same colour you add one black ball, if they are different colours you add one white ball. Eventually one ball remains. What colour is it?
puzzle.approach: Look for a quantity whose odd-or-even nature never changes, no matter which move you make.
puzzle.answer: Black. The number of white balls only ever changes by 0 or 2, so its parity is fixed; starting at 8 (even) it stays even, so the final lone ball cannot be the single (odd) white and must be black.

word_puzzle.title: Mixed Messages
word_puzzle.body: Rearrange the letters of each phrase into a single common word: 1. LISTEN (6) 2. DIRTY ROOM (9) 3. THE CLASSROOM (12).
word_puzzle.approach: Each clue's letters rearrange exactly into one ordinary word.
word_puzzle.answer: LISTEN -> SILENT; DIRTY ROOM -> DORMITORY; THE CLASSROOM -> SCHOOLMASTER.
